 Judgment
Present miscellaneous appeal has been filed assailing the award of Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) dated 24.9.2017 passed in Claim Case No. 500163/2015.

entities.text: Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The facts in brief to decide the appeal are that a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed by respondent No.1 - claimant for grant of compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in a motor accident occurred on 11.11.2015 involving bus bearing registration No. MP07-F-1882.
3. Respondents No. 2 and 3 - Driver and Owner of the offending vehicle respectively filed their written statements and denied the averments made in the claim petition and stated that since the offending vehicle is insured with appellant - insurance company, therefore, insurance company is liable to pay the compensation amount.
4. Appellant - Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied the averments made in the claim petition and
further stated that driver of the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of policy terms and conditions.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

5. Learned claims tribunal framed issues and after hearing both the parties on merits and recording their evidence allowed the claim petition of respondent No.1 - claimant and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.17,21,370/- which was directed to be paid by the respondents jointly and severely,
however, insurance company was held primary responsible to pay the compensation.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company has argued that the award passed by learned claims tribunal is against the evidence available on record.

Learned claims tribunal has erred in deciding issue No. 2 and thereby holding respondent No. 1 to have sustained 75%
permanent disability.

Learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the cases of Mangla Ram vs.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd; 2018 ACJ SC 1300 and Ramprasad vs. Anil Kumar; 2008 (4) TAC 385 SC and argued that in this case, Permanent Disability Certificate (Ex.P-1) showing permanent disability of the claimant as 75% is not proved by the issuing doctor, therefore, in the light of the above cases, learned claims tribunal has wrongly observed that there is 100% loss in earning capacity of the claimant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for respondents No. 1 to 6 - claimants opposed the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and argued that since claimant was a driver, therefore, learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed 100% loss in earning capacity of the claimant.

It is further argued that claimant has also filed cross-objection for enhancement of compensation on the ground that learned claims tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant on the lesser side.
Since claimant was driver of two vehicles, his income should have been assessed as Rs.15,000/- per month.

It is further argued that on account of accident, claimant is not able to do the work of driver because of amputation in his leg, therefore, loss of earning capacity should also have been assessed as 100%.

8. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
9.
So far as income of the claimant is concerned, he has not produced any document to show that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case as well as evidence adduced, learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed his income to be Rs.7350/-
per month.
10. Claimant has examined AW-2 S.K. Pawar, AW-3 Naval Kishore Gupta, AW-6 Asharam and AW-7 Dr. Virendra Gupta to prove the treatment of claimant in different hospitals.
The record reveals that on account of this accident, right leg of claimant got amputated from below knee.
The evidence of Dr. Virendra Gupta (AW-7) reveals that the right leg of the claimant was damaged having fractures in femur bone.
Under these circumstances, learned claims tribunal has rightly held that on account of this accident, claimant sustained permanent disability.
However, the record reveals that Permanent Disability Certificate Ex.P-1 has not been proved by the doctor who has issued the said certificate.

Therefore, without the evidence of the issuing doctor to the effect that the impact of permanent disability suffered by the claimant is 75%, learned claims tribunal has erred in holding that the claimant suffered 75% permanent disability and there would be 100% loss in the earning capacity of the claimant.

11. As discussed above, the doctor who had issued the Permanent Disability Certificate of the claimant has not been examined by the claimant, therefore, appellant - insurance company had no opportunity to cross-examine the doctor on the issue of impact of permanent disability on the earning capacity of the claimant.
Mere oral statement and visual opinion having no evidentiary value, therefore, guidance from schedule of Workmen's Compensation Act should have been taken by learned claims tribunal.

In this regard reference can be taken from the judgment passed by full Bench of this High Court in the case of Kamal Kumar Jain vs. Tajuddin & Ors.; 2004 ACJ 1191.
Therefore, in the light of the above case law, in the given situation of this case, it would be appropriate to assess the loss of earning capacity of the claimant on the basis of Workmen's Compensation Act according to which as right leg of the claimant got amputated from below knee,
50% loss in earning capacity would be applicable.

Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.; 2018 ACJ 5 SC, learned claims tribunal has rightly granted Hdfc Egro General Insurance Company ... vs Sanjeev Shakya on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91198435/

sentences.text:
13. In view of the above and in the light of case law of Pranay Sethi (supra), considering the annual income of the claimant to be Rs.88,200/-, multiplier of 17 claimant being the age group of 26-30 years, loss of income @ 50%, future prospect @ 40% and Rs.1,47,000/- towards pain and suffering,
medical expenses, attendant and special diet and transport, total compensation amount comes to Rs.11,96,580/- [Rs.7,49,700/- (88200 x 17 x 50%) + 2,99,880/- (40% future prospect on 7,49,700/-) + 1,47,000/-].
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.17,21,370/- to respondent No.1 - claimant.

The decreased amount comes to Rs.
5,24,790/- (Rupees Five Lakh Twenty Four Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety).

If the award amount has already been received by the claimant, he is directed to deposit the difference amount of Rs.5,24,790/- with interest within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award impugned passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
14. Consequently, present miscellaneous appeal cross-objection filed by respondent No. 1 - claimant is dismissed and present miscellaneous appeal is disposed of in above terms.
